failure_summary: The assembled prompt's `decision` board Tactics list asserts "double_threat at c3r6 (you, window c6r3·c5r4·c4r5·c3r6)" although c3r6 is EMPTY on the decision board (visualize_board 3321153130453320125221100544 lists only col7r4 (X) / col7r5 (O) as majors) and c3r6 is in fact the landing cell of the BLUNDER (played column 3), so the render both fabricates a decision-board tactic and invites the model to recommend the very square the player played (run 4 verbatim: "You should have played a double threat by taking the square that makes four next move" wrapping [zone:c3r6]); secondaries: `you-immediate-3`'s role string is byte-identical to `you-immediate`'s minus the "the one at c3r6:" disambiguator, which collides the same phrase onto two different squares (A7b, runs 2 and 4), the `you-double` alias's role says "the single fork square" while its spec is the 3-cell set windows:c3r6,c6r5,c7r2 that does not contain the actual pivot c5r4 (A7b/A7c), and the role/required-set strings themselves carry raw cNrM notation ("the one at c3r6", "the one through c6r3·c5r4·c4r5·c3r6") which the model echoed into player-facing prose in runs 0/1/3 (OI-194) despite the prompt's own "Never write a raw square" rule.
notes: MODEL REGIME: rows are gpt-5.4-mini, production's own model — this is a production-fidelity run, not a floor test, so no finding here is attributed to prompt_confusion; all attributions are model-independent (a false rendered tactic, two aliases with colliding role text, a role/spec mismatch, raw notation in the render's own strings). A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_subset_2026-08-26T15-47-56Z_mechanical.json (A6 fails on runs 2 and 4: prose never names column 5). Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 scored on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null (not scored, not passed). annotationRepairs is [] on all 5 runs, so G7c is clean and G7a/G7b membership passed mechanically; the G7 judgment half also passes — every emitted handle wraps a phrase that matches its (defective) role text, so the model is faithful to a broken role, not misusing a sound one. A5 fail runs 0/1/3: player-facing mechanism prose contains raw cell notation — run 0 "the c3r6 square"/"the c5r4 square", run 1 "the key reply at c5r4", run 3 "running through c6r3, c5r4, c4r5, and c3r6" and "let your opponent take c5r4"; the render supplied that notation in the alias roles, so triage is render_bug (OI-194), not model voice. A5b N/A (player === 1). A7c fail runs 0/1/2/4: the mechanism is a fork, but the square that CREATES it — c5r4, the better move's landing cell per the prompt's own Decision block "Better move: column 5 (lands at c5r4)" — is never named as the fork-making move; there is NO *-fork-pivot handle in render_decision.zones.aliases, and the only handle offered for the fork (you-double) points at the two finishing squares plus c7r2 instead, so this is a render/offer gap, not a model omission. Run 3 is the sole A7 pass because it names "column 5" as the move. A7b fail runs 2/4: the identical phrase "the square where you can make four next move" / "the square that makes four next move" is used for c3r6 AND c5r4 in the same answer — traceable to the two identical alias roles. A7b fail run 0: the singular phrase "that fork square" is bound to [zone:windows:c3r6,c6r5,c7r2], three squares, none of them the pivot. G5 fail (runs 0-1 scored): the decision-board Tactics entry above. G4 pass: every named cell traces to render_decision.finalMovestring 332115313045332012522110054424 or to a real major threat on the afterBest board 33211531304533201252211005444 (c3r6 [GT], c6r5 [GT], c7r2) — no alternate PV was used. G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard is null and L1's guardrail matches route realized_denied / direction missed_own; G2a pass, all five runs attribute the double threat to the player. G3 pass: projectedDeep shown:false is correct, the register is immediate. Known-open issues observed and not re-filed: OI-194 (raw cNrM), OI-183 (single-call harness — runs 2 and 4 omit the better column, which production's retry would have caught, so those two A6 fails are partly an eval artifact).
